purpose: Independent simulated beginner report using the fixed question set; findings are limited to visible UI observations.
persona: Simulated first-time RILL beginner interested in a short melodic instrumental.

rating_reasons.easy_to_use: Completed composition, naming, saving, exports and every requested Mixer action through visible mouse controls. The Duplicate button initially behaved differently from my expectation, and exact trimming needed a second drag.
rating_reasons.how_cool_it_looks: The dark teal arrangement, clear waveforms, note preview and mixer strips looked coherent and readable. Some mixer space was sparse, and the native save dialogs looked visually separate.
rating_reasons.how_fast_it_is: Instrument assignment, generated notes, duplicates and Mixer changes appeared promptly. WAV export showed elapsed progress and completed within the short observation interval; playback errors interrupted the flow. This is a UI impression, not a latency benchmark.
rating_reasons.how_confusing_it_is: Most labels led to the expected controls. Duplicate was a persistent tool requiring a clip click, and the first trim left 30.134 seconds instead of 30.000. Audio-stream failure banners caused uncertainty even though Retry briefly worked.
rating_reasons.feature_completeness: The requested audio, MIDI/VST, generator, mixer volume/pan, mute/solo, bus/send, naming, project save and WAV/MIDI exports were present. Playback reliability was not established, and only the single installed laboratory instrument was explored.

findings.observation: The empty-lane hint said double-click for MIDI. Double-clicking opened the Device library, where Assign instrument placed Rill Lab Sine on a new MIDI track with a pattern.

Generate notes offered Melody with a visible preview. The Length 123 button opened a mouse keypad; setting 14 bars and Add notes produced a populated MIDI pattern and a displayed project duration of 0:30.000.
Clicking Duplicate several times did not immediately duplicate the selected clip. The toolbar then said Click a clip to duplicate. Clicking the audio clips with that tool created consecutive copies.
The first drag of the final drum clip edge left the project at 0:30.134. A second short drag aligned it with the MIDI endpoint; later UI showed 0:30.000.
Dragging both Mixer faders changed the displayed drum level to -8.4 dB and MIDI level to -5.8 dB. Horizontal knob drags changed drum pan to L15 and MIDI pan to R16.

The first Play attempt showed Audio output stream failed or disconnected. Retry playback produced a Pause button, transport movement and visible MIDI/master meters; a later screenshot after adding a bus showed the failure banner again.
Drum Mute and MIDI Solo visibly highlighted when clicked. Both were toggled back off before export. No audible comparison was made.

Add bus immediately added a New bus strip. The MIDI Add send button opened routing; + Send offered New bus. Selecting it created a 0.25x Post send, and the final Mixer showed Bus 1 in and Send · New bus.

File > Rename project exposed a Keyboard control. Clicking its keys entered glow. Save as prefilled glow.rill in the session-3 folder, and accepting the dialog returned to the project. A later File > Save also returned without an error.

WAV export displayed Arrangement · 0:30. I unchecked Include effect tails, accepted glow.wav in session-3, and saw Exported · glow.wav. Export MIDI likewise prefilled glow.mid and showed Exported · glow.mid.

outcome.status: Completed via the visible UI: named and saved a 30.000-second arrangement, obtained WAV and MIDI export success notices, and performed all requested Mixer actions. File contents and sound remain for independent verification.
outcome.composition: 112 BPM, 4/4 melodic instrumental: startup Circuit rhythm audio duplicated to four consecutive clips with the last trimmed to the 30-second endpoint, plus a 14-bar C-major-triad Random walk melody generated in a MIDI pattern. Added one bus with a 0.25x post send from the MIDI track.
outcome.playback_observed: Initial Play produced an audio-stream failure banner. Retry playback showed Pause, a transport value of 001.01.39 and active MIDI/master meters. Later the transport was at 003.02.94 with another failure banner. Playback was stopped and returned to the start before exports. This does not establish continuous 30-second playback or heard audio.

limitations: No file contents were inspected and no audio capture was auditioned; output paths come from visible save dialogs. Independent coordinator verification follows.
Volume and pan changes were made visually, not judged by listening. Mute/solo button states were observed without an audible comparison.
The laboratory uses software graphics and a timer-paced virtual audio sink with 60 ms buffering; the stream failures and perceived speed cannot be generalized to physical hardware.
Only Rill Lab Sine was available and explored; no conclusions about other VST instruments.
The native save dialogs briefly appeared as black rectangles before rendering on a later screenshot. Session elapsed time includes screenshots, tools and reporting overhead.

mixer_outcome.volume: Dragged drum fader from -6.0 to -8.4 dB and MIDI fader from -2.5 to -5.8 dB; both values remained visible in the final Mixer.
mixer_outcome.pan: Dragged drum knob horizontally to L15 and MIDI knob to R16; both values remained visible in the final Mixer.
mixer_outcome.mute: Clicked drum Mute on; amber highlighting appeared. Clicked it off before export. Audible muting unverified.
mixer_outcome.solo: Clicked MIDI Solo on; teal highlighting appeared, with MIDI/master meters active after playback retry. Clicked it off before export. Audible isolation unverified.
mixer_outcome.bus: Clicked Add bus; New bus strip appeared with 0.0 dB, center pan and output Ch 3 > Master. Final strip showed Bus 1 in.
mixer_outcome.send: Clicked MIDI Add send, then + Send, then New bus. Routing displayed New bus at 0.25x with Post selected. Final Mixer showed Send · New bus on the MIDI strip.
